data.title: IndusInd Bank shares jump 8% on volume surge, near 52-week high
data.description:
Shares of IndusInd Bank rose over 8 per cent on Friday after the company's counter saw a strong volume surge amid traction in banking stocks. Today's rally also pushed the stock close to its 52-week high of 1,077.85.
 
The bank’s counter at 03:07 PM was trading 8.2 per cent higher at ₹999.90 per share on NSE. In comparison, Nifty 50 was up 1.10 per cent at 25,360.85. In intraday trade, the stock rose 8.4 per cent to touch the day's high at ₹1,001 per share.
 
IndusInd Bank recorded a traded volume of 182.05 lakh shares, with a total traded value of ₹1,786.52 crore. The bank's total market capitalisation stood at ₹77,856.04 crore, while its free-float market capitalisation was ₹65,709.17 crore.
 
 
Notably, the Nifty Bank index hit a new high of 64,636, gaining nearly 2.5 per cent on the National Stock Exchange in Friday’s intraday deals, surging over 3 per cent in the past two trading days. 
 
IndusInd Bank Q2 show 
IndusInd Bank posted a sequential improvement in business momentum, profitability and asset quality, even as net interest margins moderated during the second quarter of FY27. The bank reported a 9 per cent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) increase in average total loans, while average deposits grew 7 per cent. Its loan book stood at ₹3.63 trillion at the end of September 2026, up 11 per cent year-on-year, while deposits rose 10 per cent to ₹4.29 trillion.
 
The bank said asset quality continued to improve, with moderation in stressed loan pools and lower slippages. Gross non-performing assets (GNPA) declined to 2.73 per cent in Q2 FY27 from 3.25 per cent in the previous quarter, while net NPAs fell to 0.83 per cent from 0.95 per cent. Fresh NPA additions also declined to ₹1,460 crore from ₹1,660 crore in Q1 FY27. The bank's provision coverage ratio stood at 70 per cent, while its restructured book reduced to 0.04 per cent of net advances.
 
Vipin Kumar, AVP research at Globe Capital Market, said that IndusInd Bank is moving in a higher highs and higher lows formation within an upward-sloping channel formation since May 2025. Today, it witnessed a bullish break from a 10-day congestion range and also crossed above the gap zone left during its fall on September 24, 2026. “Going ahead, we expect it to test the ₹1,050–₹1,100 levels in the near term, which also represents the upper band of the channel formation,” he said. 
 
Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: Is Tony Stark no longer Iron Man? Marvel announces new version of superhero
data.description:
Tony Stark is set to undergo one of his most disturbing transformations in Marvel's comic-book universe. The superhero, best known for his high-tech red-and-gold armour, is being reimagined as a monstrous creature called 'The Iron Thing'.
 
In the upcoming comic series Hulk War: Infernal Rage, Tony Stark modifies into ‘The Iron Thing.’ Although the character is still fundamentally Tony Stark, he has been altered by the Infernal Hulk and does not represent a new hero taking over the suit.

How does Tony Stark become the 'Iron Thing'?

In the upcoming story, Tony Stark is defeated by the Infernal Hulk despite wearing his powerful Hellbuster armour and wielding a spear associated with the One Above All, Marvel's supreme cosmic entity. 
 
 
Following his defeat, Stark becomes one of the Infernal Hulk's first monstrous recruits. His familiar Iron Man appearance is replaced by a grotesque form that bears little resemblance to the armoured superhero.
 
The new Stark is shown as a huge, misshapen creature, even bulkier than the Hulk, with a simple grey mask concealing his face. His advanced armour is no longer the defining feature of the role. Instead, the transformation appears to sacrifice much of his intellectual prowess in favour of overwhelming physical strength. 
 
The new design also caught the attention of artist Nic Klein, who is working on the series. Speaking about the monstrous group, Klein elaborated the Iron Thing as a “huge, gross, veiny lump of flesh and muscle,” adding that it can be his favourite of the Infernal Avengers to attract.

Does this mean Iron Man is being replaced in the MCU?

No. The Iron Thing represents progress within the Marvel comic universe and currently has no confirmed ties to the storyline of the MCU's films or TV shows. Robert Downey Jr., known for his role as Tony Stark in the MCU, is expected to make a comeback in Marvel's cinematic universe in Avengers: Doomsday, but he will take on the role of Doctor Doom this time. The release date for the film is set for December 18, 2026. 

What happened to the other Avengers?

Iron Man is not the only hero in the Avengers to experience a significant evolution. The Infernal Hulk's group also features terrifying renditions of Spider-Man and Captain America. Additional well-known heroes have received strange new looks as well. Captain Marvel changes into a creature resembling a bird with a skull for a face, whereas Jubilee turns into a radiant being composed solely of energy. 
 
Vision's transformation is equally unusual. The android hero is now shown as a huge brain contained within a robotic frame, sporting a large eye and wings that lend him a nearly angelic look.  
Tony Stark has explored numerous versions of his armour in the past, such as those used for battling the Hulk, Thor, and Galactus. Nevertheless, his recent transformation goes well beyond mere enhancements in technology.

When will Hulk War: Infernal Rage release?

Hulk War: Infernal Rage is a comic-book series consisting of 5 issues, crafted by Phillip Kennedy Johnson with illustrations by Nic Klein. The pair has collaborated before on The Infernal Hulk. 
 
The first issue of the series is scheduled to arrive in comic-book stores on February 3, 2027.

data.title: Russian strikes on Kyiv kill three, injure nine and disrupt power supply
data.description:
Russia launched missiles and drones across Kyiv overnight that killed three people, injured nine others and damaged bridges and transport infrastructure, local authorities said Friday.

The attacks came hours after President Vladimir Putin vowed to retaliate against Ukraine for three aerial attacks this week on the vital Kerch Bridge, which links occupied Crimea with the Russian mainland.

"We will respond to these attacks, and I want everyone to be clear about that," Putin told reporters Thursday in China, where he attended a summit with the Chinese and US presidents. Putin said the road side of the bridge had been "seriously damaged" and vowed to rebuild.

 

The Kyiv City Military Administration said the attack struck four districts of the capital. The attack caused widespread electricity disruptions. Energy provider DTEK said parts of the Pecherskyi, Solomianskyi, Holosiivskyi, Dniprovskyi and Darnytskyi districts were without power following the strikes.

Non-residential buildings were damaged in the Obolonskyi and Holosiivskyi districts, while transport and logistics infrastructure was hit in the Podilskyi and Darnytskyi districts, it said in a statement.

Kyiv's Mayor Vitali Klitschko said a ballistic missile attack damaged the Podilskyi Bridge, forcing authorities to close traffic from the right bank to the left bank of the Dnipro River.

The Darnitskyi Bridge was also damaged, he said.

A further strike hit the Southern Bridge, where traffic remains restricted. Only vehicles weighing up to 10 tonnes travelling from the left bank to the right bank, and public transport weighing up to 18 tons, are being permitted, he said.

Klitschko urged residents to avoid travelling into the city by private car unless absolutely necessary. He asked businesses and institutions to arrange remote working wherever possible.

data.title: Premium smartphone prices may rise over 30% by year-end: Counterpoint
data.description:
Prices of premium flagship smartphones are expected to go up by 30 per cent to over ₹1 lakh apiece across most of the brands by end of the year due to a sharp rise in memory chip cost, market research firm Counterpoint said on Friday.

Along with the increase in prices of the devices, consumer expectations are also rising, and consumers are looking for meaningful specifications that can match the desired experience across processing speed of the mobile phones, camera, battery, durability, after-sales service, etc.

"A few years ago, a ₹1-lakh smartphone was a rarity in India. Today, as flagship prices keep rising, this price point is becoming increasingly common. Prices of premium flagship devices are expected to rise by more than 30 per cent by the end of 2026 compared with 2025," Counterpoint Research said in a report.

 

Memory prices are expected to account for 43 per cent of the total phone cost by year-end compared to 13 per cent in the first quarter of 2025, as per the report.

"Rising DRAM (temporary storage) and NAND costs, driven by AI data centre demand, have pushed memory's share of smartphone BOM (bill of materials) from about 13 per cent in early 2025 to over 40 per cent, prompting smartphone manufacturers to reassess specifications, components and product strategies to manage costs," said Tarun Pathak, Research Director, Counterpoint Research.

According to the report, Oppo flagship devices have seen the highest jump in the range of 82-87 per cent on a year-over-year (YoY) basis.

Ultra-premium segment market leader iPhone prices have gone up by 20-22 per cent YoY.

"There is no single best premium flagship, as consumer priorities vary. As Apple and Samsung flagship prices move towards ₹2 lakh, tech-focused brands like iQOO and Google are attracting consumers with specifications that are at par but at more competitive prices. Beyond hardware, ecosystem flexibility is becoming an important differentiator, especially for working professionals who tend to carry more than one smartphone in addition to a laptop," the report said.

Market leader Samsung recently increased the price of smartphones in the range of ₹2,000-₹4,000 apiece post Diwali.

Before Diwali, the firm had raised the price of its flagship device Galaxy S26 by 17 per cent.

Chinese smartphone company Xiaomi has also increased the price of devices in the same range after Diwali.

data.title: 74 out of every 100 consumer loan applications were for phones this Diwali
data.description:
India's festive shopping season is increasingly being financed by credit, with consumer-durable loan applications rising 22% during Diwali 2026 compared with last year, even as demand shifts towards smaller towns and rural markets.
 
Data from lending technology platform Lentra for November 1-9, 2026, show that rural India accounted for 58% of consumer-durable loan applications, compared with 42% from urban India. Tier-3 towns also edged past metropolitan cities, pointing to a widening geographical base for consumption financed through borrowing.
 
The numbers suggest that festive credit demand is no longer concentrated in large cities. Smaller towns and rural markets are emerging as important drivers of purchases ranging from smartphones and televisions to refrigerators and washing machines.
 
 
The average consumer-durable loan ticket size stood at an estimated Rs 28,000, indicating the scale of purchases being financed through credit. 
Diwali 2026: What India's Credit-Fuelled Purchases Looked Like Across States
 
 Young Indians lead festive borrowing
 
The age profile of borrowers highlights the growing importance of younger consumers in the festive credit market. Around 62% of consumer-durable loan applicants were below 35, with the 22-35 age group emerging as the typical borrower segment.
 
Mobile phones dominated the borrowing basket. Nearly 74 out of every 100 consumer-durable loan applications were for mobile phones, while the remaining 26 were spread across other categories of consumer durables.
 
The concentration of demand in smartphones points to their continued importance as a primary consumption purchase among younger borrowers. Men aged 22-25 were particularly prominent in mobile-phone financing, according to Lentra's analysis.
 
However, the pattern changes when gender and age are considered together. Women showed a stronger preference for financing household appliances, particularly in the 35-plus age group.
 
Women's borrowing patterns reveal a different consumption story
 
Women accounted for 31% of consumer-durable loan buyers in urban areas, compared with 24% in rural markets.
 
The difference suggests that women's participation in credit-financed consumption remains higher in cities, although their share of borrowing in rural markets is also significant.
 
The data also point towards a different product preference among women. While men typically borrowed for mobile phones, appliance purchases were more prominent among women aged 35 and above.
 
Women's two-wheeler borrowing provides another insight into changing consumption aspirations. Of every 100 women's two-wheeler loan applications across city tiers, 57 were for motorcycles, 39 for scooters and mopeds, and four for electric two-wheelers.
 
 India's festive shopping basket changes from state to state
 
The state-level numbers reveal how consumption preferences vary significantly across markets.
 
Gujarat and Rajasthan were particularly smartphone-driven markets. Mobile phones accounted for 86% of consumer-durable loan applications in Gujarat, compared with the national average of 74%. In Rajasthan, the share stood at 82%.
 
Television financing was more prominent in southern India. LED TVs accounted for 13.6% of consumer-durable loan applications in Telangana and 12.4% in Tamil Nadu, against a national average of 7.4%.
 
Refrigerators featured more prominently in eastern and southern markets. They accounted for 6.8% of applications in West Bengal and 6.6% in Karnataka, compared with the national average of 4.6%. Madhya Pradesh also recorded a higher share at 6.1%.
 
In northern India, washing machines emerged as a stronger category. They accounted for 15% of consumer-durable loan applications in Punjab, against the national average of 4%. Haryana recorded an 8.3% share, while Delhi stood at 6%.
 
The data also reveal distinct demand patterns in other states. Air conditioners accounted for 6% of applications in Andhra Pradesh, 2.5 times the national share of 2.4%. Maharashtra stood out for audio systems, which accounted for 2.1% of applications compared with the national average of 1.6%.
 
In Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, inverters and batteries had a higher share of applications at 1.3% and 1.1%, respectively, compared with the national average of 0.6%.
 
Key highlights: 
 
  • Mobile phones lead festive consumer-durable financing with a 74% national share
  • Gujarat and Rajasthan lead in mobile phone financing, with the category accounting for 86% and 82% of applications, respectively.
  • Southern states show a stronger preference for LED TVs, while refrigerators and washing machines feature more prominently across several other markets.
  • Consumer-durable loan applications grew 22% over the previous festive period, with rural markets accounting for 58% of applications.
  • In Telangana and Tamil Nadu, LED televisions accounted for a notably higher proportion of applications than rest of the states. 
  • Telangana recorded a 13.6% share, followed by Tamil Nadu at 12.4%.
  • Refrigerators featured more prominently across West Bengal, Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh, accounting for 6.8%, 6.6% and 6.1% of applications, respectively.
  • In Punjab, washing machines accounted for 15% of consumer-durable loan applications. Haryana recorded an 8.3% share, while Delhi stood at 6%.
  • In Andhra Pradesh, air conditioners accounted for 6% of applications, 2.4%. Maharashtra recorded a relatively higher share of audio system financing at 2.1%
  • In Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, inverters and batteries accounted for 1.3% and 1.1% of applications
 
" India does not have one festive shopping basket. What is significant is where this demand is coming from. With rural markets contributing 58% of applications and Tier-3 towns edging past metros, festive credit activity is clearly extending beyond the largest cities," said Rajesh Kumar, CEO, Lentra.

data.title: Explained: Sarvam AI's Token Factory and debate over AI sovereignty goals
data.description:
Indian artificial intelligence startup Sarvam AI has announced Token Factory, offering access to multiple models, including its own and those developed in China, through a unified inference platform. The announcement has sparked debate over India's homegrown AI ambitions. The matter has come under scrutiny because Sarvam is among the companies selected under the government's IndiaAI Mission to develop homegrown AI models.

What is Sarvam AI’s Token Factory

Sarvam AI’s Token Factory is a platform that allows businesses and developers to use different artificial intelligence (AI) models through a single service, without having to set up or manage their own computing infrastructure. According to the company, it runs Sarvam’s own AI models as well as other open-weight models, including DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi and Google’s Gemma, on GPU clusters located in India. Users can access these models through a single application programming interface (API), which allows their applications to connect to the AI service and send requests.
 
 
The platform handles the process of running an AI model and generating responses to users’ questions or instructions. This process is called inference. Sarvam says its system is designed to make this process faster and more cost-effective by managing how requests are sent to its GPUs and reusing parts of earlier prompts where possible. Businesses can choose a model depending on their requirements and pay based on the number of tokens processed. Tokens are small units of text that an AI model reads or generates.

How Sarvam’s Token Factory functions

Sarvam describes Token Factory as an inference stack serving its own and other open-weight models from GPU clusters in India. Its catalogue includes Sarvam 105B, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and V4 Pro, Kimi K3.1 Pro, GLM 5.3 and Flash, and Gemma 4 31B. Developers access them through one OpenAI-compatible API by configuring the endpoint, selecting a model and sending requests.
 
The platform manages the work between a request and a response through three layers:
  • An inference engine
  • A cache
  • A control plane
The engine runs the model on graphics processing units (GPUs). The cache stores reusable prompt information to avoid processing the same context repeatedly. The control plane manages requests, routes them to the appropriate resources and adjusts capacity according to demand.
 
The engine separates processing into prefill and decode. Prefill reads the full prompt, including earlier conversation or context. Decode generates the answer one token at a time. Sarvam says these tasks run on separate GPU pools because they have different computing requirements. This can prevent long prompts from slowing response generation for other users.
 
Caching is useful in long conversations and AI agent workflows, where a model may receive the same context repeatedly. Without it, the system processes those tokens again, adding cost and delay. Sarvam says its multi-tier cache uses GPU memory and shared storage to reuse prompt information. A cache-aware router can direct returning requests to servers where relevant context is available.
 
Sarvam charges for input, cached input and output tokens, with rates varying by model and listed in rupees per million tokens. It says it serves more than 450 billion tokens a day through DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. The aim is to provide access to several models without requiring customers to maintain the underlying infrastructure. 
ALSO READ: AI is giving hackers a head start. What's at risk for essential services?

Why has Token Factory triggered a sovereignty debate

The central criticism is that a model’s country of origin differs from the country where it is hosted. DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM were developed by Chinese companies. Running their open-weight versions on Indian GPUs does not make them Indian, transfer their intellectual property to Sarvam or give India control over their development. This raises the question of whether India is building its own AI capabilities or mainly providing infrastructure to run models developed elsewhere.
 
The term covers the ability to set rules for how AI systems are developed and used, audit their behaviour, protect sensitive information and maintain access to critical computing resources. It is therefore broader than data localisation or the nationality of a model developer.
 
Sarvam’s role in India’s AI ecosystem has intensified the debate. It was selected under the IndiaAI Mission, which seeks to strengthen domestic AI capabilities, including indigenous foundation models, and received subsidised computing resources to train its own models. This has raised questions about whether government support for developing homegrown AI was also benefiting a commercial platform offering access to Chinese AI models.
 
Sarvam said its Token Factory does not use government-subsidised GPUs. Co-founder Pratyush Kumar told Moneycontrol that the platform runs on privately procured GPUs. The company said its subsidised access under the IndiaAI Mission, used to train its own models, ended in March 2026. It maintains that developing its own models remains its core mission, while offering other models generates revenue.
 
According to the report, Sarvam argues that model development is expensive and inference can generate revenue from computing infrastructure. It says Indian businesses should be able to use global models through a domestic provider, with local infrastructure and rupee pricing. Global cloud providers such as Amazon Web Services also offer businesses access to AI models developed by other companies through platforms such as Amazon Bedrock.
 
Data sovereignty is another concern. Sarvam says Token Factory runs AI models on its GPU infrastructure in India and does not send customer prompts to the overseas providers that developed those models. The company also says it offers zero data retention on request, under which prompts and responses are not stored. However, keeping data in India does not automatically address every security concern.
 
Businesses also need to examine how data is accessed, how long it is retained and what security measures are in place. Hosting a foreign-developed model in India also does not make the model indigenous.

What about other Indian AI platforms

Sarvam AI has faced greater criticism not only because it is hosting Chinese AI models. Other Indian companies, including E2E Networks and IndieRouter, also offer access to foreign-developed models through infrastructure located in India. E2E Networks, for instance, launched its Blaze inference platform on November 2, 2026, offering models such as DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM and Gemma through a single API. However, Sarvam's position is different because it was selected under the government's IndiaAI Mission to develop indigenous foundation models and has been seen as an important part of India's effort to build its own AI technology.
 
The criticism has therefore centred on whether a company backed by the government to develop homegrown AI should also build a commercial business around models developed in other countries, particularly China. The Indian Express reported that the reaction was partly driven by the expectations attached to Sarvam as a symbol of India's AI ambitions. Supporters, however, argue that hosting foreign models can be a business opportunity and allow Indian companies to serve customers using locally available computing infrastructure.

 

ALSO READ: AI is giving hackers a head start. What's at risk for essential services?
 How does hosting foreign models benefit Sarvam
Chinese AI companies have developed several powerful open-weight models, including DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM. Unlike some AI services that can only be accessed through a company's own platform, open-weight models can be downloaded and run on a company's own servers. This makes them an option for businesses that want to use advanced AI models without relying on services such as OpenAI or Anthropic.
 
For Sarvam, offering these models gives it another source of business besides developing its own AI models. It can attract companies that want to use models such as DeepSeek or Kimi but do not have the GPUs or technical resources to run them themselves. Sarvam provides the computing infrastructure and access through its Token Factory platform.

data.title: Textiles shares hit new high; Indo Count, Welspun Living rally up to 8%
data.description:
Textile shares price movement

 
Shares of textile companies were in demand, rallying up to 8 per cent on the BSE in Friday’s intraday deals amid heavy volume on strong earnings and a healthy business outlook.
 
Welspun Living’s share price soared 8 per cent to hit a new high of ₹274 in intraday deals. Share price of Pearl Global Industries also hit a new high of ₹1,469, surging 5 per cent. Nitin Spinners (₹721.75) and Indo Count Industries (₹594) also hit their respective all-time highs, and were up 4 per cent and 3 per cent, respectively. In comparison, the BSE Sensex was up 1 per cent at 83,865 at 02:14 PM.
 
 
In the past month, the stock price of Indo Count Industries zoomed 45 per cent, followed by Welspun Living (29 per cent), Pearl Global Industries (21 per cent) and Nitin Spinners (11 per cent). The BSE Sensex rallied 14 per cent during the same period.
 

What’s driving textile stocks?

 
The textile sector in the July to September 2026 quarter (Q2FY27) results delivered 26 per cent year-on-year (YoY) growth, supported by higher order execution and demand recovery. Analysts at Motilal Oswal Financial Services expect the sector to sustain its outperformance, with an over 15 per cent growth and gradual margin recovery for fabric/apparel/home textile players. In contrast, margins for spinning players are expected to normalize as cotton yarn spreads revert to normal levels. Key monitorables include cotton prices, freight and fuel costs, and order flows from the US and Europe. 
 
The brokerage firm expects its coverage to grow 17 per cent, 31 per cent, and 52 per cent, respectively, over FY26-28. Accordingly, analysts have assigned a 15 per cent premium to the mean P/E multiple. They prefer Gokaldas Export, Pearl Global, and Arvind from the apparel space and Indo Count Industries from the home textile space.
 
Meanwhile, India is fast securing multiple bilateral agreements with preferential tariffs, reducing the 10-12 per cent duty gap in key markets such as the UK and EU. Along with the narrowing tariff differential, Bangladesh is facing challenges related to raw material and energy security – leading to the disruption of operations/increased costs, especially for smaller players. Despite these setbacks, the country’s highly evolved textile ecosystem and low-cost labour market continue to give it an edge. However, the recent protests – with workers demanding more than double the current wages – threaten to reduce the country’s advantage on the labour cost front, analysts at PL Capital said in its textile sector update.
 
Meanwhile, in Q2FY27, Indo Count Industries’ earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) more than doubled to ₹259 crore on a year-on-year (YoY) basis from ₹123 crore, with margins expanding to 15.3 per cent, well above the company’s full-year guidance of 13 per cent. The performance was driven by market share gains, increased wallet share, strong branded business momentum, and increasing contribution from the company’s newer businesses.
 
Indo Count Industries in its Q2 earnings conference call said that the UK and EU markets offer significant growth potential, with an addressable opportunity comparable to the US market. The company’s established relationships with leading retailers provide a strong platform to expand presence and increase wallet share. The company also expects free trade agreements to further strengthen its competitiveness in these markets.
 
“Overall, the combination of strong growth across our businesses, improving margins, and a strong balance sheet positioned us well and gives us confidence in outperforming our FY27 guidance,” the management said. Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

data.title: RBI clarifies forex reporting rules for services imports and exports
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India on Friday clarified the scope of foreign ​exchange reporting rules governing services imports ​and exports that went into effect in October ‌and sparked questions about whether they apply to resident individuals.

Earlier this month, the central bank had exempted resident individuals from declaration requirements and introduced a threshold of ₹10 lakh ($10,760.79) for certain reporting obligations.

The RBI on Friday issued a set of frequently asked questions governing services trade transactions. Here are some details:

The central ‌bank clarified that the ₹10 lakh threshold applies to each inward remittance and not the aggregate amount of receipts.

Non-individual service exporters receiving over ₹10 lakh are required to file an export declaration form (EDF) before the credit of proceeds.

 

Authorized banks ​can extend EDF filing deadlines if they consider exporters' reasons to ‌be justified. Banks will be required to publish trade-related policies and key operating procedures ​on ‌their websites.

The RBI notified the original rules governing reporting ‌requirements in January, and they went into effect on October 1.

"These new regulations are designed to ‌align ​with evolving global ​trade practices and aim to significantly enhance the ease of doing business," it said in ‌a Friday ​statement.

data.title: Contra funds get NFO boost: Is it time to bet against the market consensus?
data.description:
The contra fund category recorded net inflows of ₹1,694.13 crore in October 2026, compared with net outflows of ₹97.88 crore in September. At first glance, this may suggest rising investor interest. A closer look at the numbers, however, presents a more nuanced picture.
 
Around 88 per cent of the total inflows in October came from the new fund offer (NFO) of ICICI Prudential Contra Fund alone. This raises the question of whether investors are genuinely moving towards stocks and sectors that are currently out of favour with the market, or whether the surge in contra fund inflows is largely the result of one large NFO.
 
 
ICICI Prudential Contra Fund raised ₹1,488 crore through its NFO in October. This accounted for around 39 per cent of the total amount raised by all new schemes during the month. The other five schemes in the six-fund contra category together attracted net inflows of just ₹206 crore. This indicates that the October surge was not broad-based across the category.

Investors look for value beyond expensive stocks

Some investors are beginning to look beyond popular stocks and explore opportunities in companies and sectors that are currently out of favour. However, the shift remains limited.
 
A K Nigam, chief executive officer and director at BPN Fincap, said most retail investors were still chasing popular stocks. “Smallcap funds alone attracted ₹6,408 crore in October. However, a section of investors is now becoming wary of buying stocks at high valuations,” he said.
 
Nigam said that after two years of strong gains in midcap and smallcap stocks, shares of several companies were trading at price-to-earnings (P/E) ratios of more than 30 times. Investors were, therefore, looking for opportunities in relatively less-favoured sectors such as public-sector undertakings (PSUs), pharmaceuticals, fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) and banking.
 
Gurmeet Singh Chawla, managing director at Master Portfolio Services, said some investors were now looking at companies whose valuations had corrected. However, this did not mean the phase of momentum investing was over.
 
He cautioned that a stock being out of favour did not necessarily make it cheap. Investors should assess whether the company’s earnings could recover, whether its competitive position remained strong, and whether the underlying business fundamentals were sound.

Rising inflows: Confidence or NFO effect?

Nigam believes the return of inflows into contra funds reflects not just the launch of a new scheme but also some improvement in investor confidence. He said inflows into value-oriented funds had also increased, suggesting that some existing investors might have raised their exposure through systematic investment plans (SIPs) and lump-sum investments.
 
Chawla, however, said the rise in October inflows could have been driven mainly by the launch of the new scheme rather than a broadbased return of investor confidence.
 
With ₹1,488 crore coming from a single NFO, the contribution from existing schemes remained relatively modest. He said investors would need to track fresh inflows into existing schemes and SIP contributions over the coming months to determine whether interest in contra funds was genuinely increasing.

Why does a contra strategy matter in the current market?

Contra funds invest in companies and sectors that are currently out of favour with the market but have the potential to recover over time. Fund managers look for businesses whose market valuations do not adequately reflect their underlying operating strength and fundamentals.
 
Nigam said the strategy was relevant in the current market because valuations in some parts of the market had become expensive. Largecap stocks were trading at around 19 times earnings, while midcap and smallcap stocks were at around 27 times and 33 times, respectively, he said.
 
He also pointed to foreign institutional investor (FII) selling of ₹34,843 crore in October, which he said could create opportunities in good-quality companies.
 
According to Nigam, sectors such as information technology, pharmaceuticals, FMCG and banking could also offer opportunities if company fundamentals remained strong despite weak market sentiment.
 
Chawla also said contra strategies remained relevant, but urged caution. Not every beaten-down stock is worth investing in, he said. Some companies remain cheap because of weakening market share, poor balance sheets or weak business models.

How long should investors stay invested?

Contra investing requires patience because it can take years for the market to recognise the true potential of an overlooked company.
 
Nigam recommends an investment horizon of at least five years and, for better results, up to seven years. The first one or two years can be difficult, he said, as fund managers invest in stocks that are out of favour and the fund may underperform its benchmark.
 
Over the next three to five years, however, business conditions could improve and stock valuations could rise through a rerating.
 
Chawla also recommended an investment horizon of at least five to seven years. Improvements in earnings, changes in industry conditions and shifts in market sentiment can take time, he said.
 
Investors who cannot tolerate prolonged periods of underperformance may find it difficult to remain invested in such a strategy.

What should existing investors do?

Existing investors should not take decisions based solely on one month’s flow data.
 
Nigam advised investors against redeeming in panic. Those who invested in contra funds one or two years ago and were currently seeing weak performance could continue their SIPs if the fund’s strategy and portfolio remained aligned with their financial goals.
 
Investors who have stayed invested for four or five years and earned good returns could also continue holding. However, if contra funds have grown to more than 20 per cent of their overall portfolio, they may consider booking some profits.
 
Nigam cautioned investors against committing fresh money aggressively merely because inflows into the category had increased.
 
Chawla also said SIPs could continue if the fund’s portfolio and strategy remained consistent with the investor’s financial goals. However, any additional investment should be based on stock valuations, earnings prospects and the quality of the underlying businesses.
 
Investors should also examine how much their contra fund portfolio overlaps with their other equity funds. If the same stocks have high weights across funds, the diversification benefit may be limited.

How much should contra funds account for in a portfolio?

Nigam suggested allocating 10-15 per cent of an equity portfolio to contra funds. For investors with a long investment horizon and greater risk tolerance, the allocation could go up to a maximum of 20 per cent.
 
Chawla took a more conservative view, suggesting that contra funds account for around 5-10 per cent of the equity portfolio. This, he said, could allow investors to benefit from the strategy without creating excessive concentration risk.

data.title: DGCA issues show cause notice to SpiceJet over flight cancellations, delays
data.description:
Aviation watchdog DGCA has issued a show cause notice to crisis-hit SpiceJet seeking detailed responses on rising flight cancellations, operational disruptions due to delayed payments and certain violations, according to sources.

The budget carrier, which saw its domestic market share dip to 0.6 per cent in September from 1.2 per cent in August, has been witnessing significant operational issues resulting in flight delays and cancellations.

The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has sought explanations from SpiceJet on the continued deterioration in operational performance, reflected in significantly declining OnTime Performance (OTP), increasing flight delays and growing flight cancellations.

In the show cause notice dated November 17, the regulator also flagged the airline's non-adherence to approved schedule, persistent passenger inconvenience arising from flight disruptions, cancellations, delays and inadequate passenger facilitation measures.

 

The airline has been directed to reply within seven days from the date of the issuance of the show cause notice.

"... the majority of the aircraft fleet of SpiceJet is grounded and the airline has failed to submit a credible plan for return to service of the grounded aircraft," the DGCA said in the show cause notice.

Besides, the watchdog has mentioned about uncertainty regarding renewal of mandatory insurance coverage and concerns raised by overseas aviation authorities regarding operational disruptions linked to delayed payments to service providers.

DGCA has also asked an explanation from the airline for non-payment of penalty imposed by it earlier despite repeated reminders.

According to the show cause notice, the airline has failed to comply with eligibility requirements for scheduled international operations and has repeatedly failed to comply with Route Dispersal Guidelines (RDG) despite previous enforcement action and imposition of penalty in May.

Details about the earlier penalty could not be immediately ascertained.

There was no immediate comment from SpiceJet on the show cause notice.

The show cause notice was issued on November 17, a day before SpiceJet's board approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 5,500 crore to shore up its financial position.

Shares of the carrier fell nearly 5 per cent to Rs 9.74 in afternoon trade on the BSE.

BSE has sought a clarification from the airline regarding reports about the DGCA show cause notice.

For the second straight day on Friday, Delhi airport operator DIAL, in a post on X, said that due to operational challenge being faced by SpiceJet, some flights may be impacted.
